Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant, calling in question the judgment and award dated 10.07.2017, passed in M.V.C.No.788/2015, on the file of the Additional District And Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Kundapura, Udupi District, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

Brief facts:
2. On 02.06.2015, at about 4.30 p.m., the claimant was travelling as a passenger in an Auto Rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-20-C-896, from Bantwady side towards Mullikate side, when the said Auto rickshaw reached near Government Higher Primary School Hosadu, a Bus bearing registration No.KA-20-C-7065, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner in a bid to overtake the auto-rickshaw by seeing the upcoming vehicle from the opposite site, he suddenly turned to the left side from the right side without given any signal and dashed against the said auto-rickshaw.
Due the said impact the claimant fell down and sustained injuries all over the body.

sentences.text: Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant- claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part,
and awarded a compensation of Rs.1,52,121/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent Nos.2 and 3 therein, jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.3 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.
5.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
1. Injury, Pain and Sufferings : Rs. 50,000/-
2. Medical Expenses : Rs. 13,269/-
3. Loss of Earning during bed rest : Rs. 932/-
4. Bed Rest : Rs. 28,000/-
5. Loss of Future earning capacity : Rs. 52,920/-
6. Conveyance, Nourishment and : Rs. 7,000/-
attendant charges TOTAL : Rs. 1,52,121/-
6.
Therefore, considering this, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'Pain and Sufferings, at Rs.50,000/-, is found to be correct and hence kept in-tact.
8. The claimant was aged 60 years and the accident has occurred during the year 2015.
The Tribunal has held the income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/- per month, which is on lesser side.
Therefore, as Sri. Krishnappa Shetty vs Sri.Prathap Shetty on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157696932/

sentences.text: 3 per Chart of notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, a sum of Rs.9,000/- is to be taken as notional monthly income of the claimant.
The Doctor had stated the claimant had suffered 14% functional disability with respect to the right hand and 7% towards the whole- body.
The criteria for calculating functional disability is elaborately discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another1

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, considering the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court stated supra, and the injuries suffered by the appellant and the avocation of the appellant-claimant being Mason, certainly the disability will affect his earning capacity.
Accordingly, 7% functional disability to the whole-body as assessed by the Doctor is taken.
The appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others.
Vs. Delhi Transport Corpn And Another2 is '9'.

Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss of Earning Capacity Due to Disability' is recalculated and quantified as follows:
(2011) 1 SCC 343 AIR 2009 SC 3104 Rs.9,000/- x 7% x 9 x 12 = Rs.68,040/-
9.
In view of the accidental injuries, the claimant would have taken rest for atleast for a period of Four months.

Therefore, by taking income at Rs.9,000/- per month and calculating the laid up period for Four months, the claimant is entitled for a sum of Rs.36,000/- (Rs.9,000 x 4 months),
under the head 'Loss Of Earning During Laid Up Period'.
10.
The Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards 'Loss Of Amenities', hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the said head.

11. The Tribunal has awarded compensation towards 'Food, Nourishment, Conveyance and Attendant Charges' at Rs.7,000/-, which is on lesser side and hence a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the said head.

12. The compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal under the 'Medical Expenses' at Rs.13,269/-
is as per actual bills and receipts and the same is kept in tact.

13. Therefore, in modification of the award of the Tribunal, the appellant-claimant is entitled to the following compensation:
1. Injury, Pain and Sufferings : Rs. 50,000/-
2. Medical Expenses : Rs. 13,269/-
3. Loss of Earning during Laid Off : Rs. 36,000/-
Period (Rs.9,000 x 4 months)
4. Loss of Future earning capacity : Rs. 68,040/-
(Rs.9,000 x 7% x 9 x 12)

4 5. Conveyance, Nourishment and : Rs. 15,000/-
attendant charges

6. Loss of Amenities : Rs. 25,000/-
TOTAL : Rs. 2,07,309/-
14.
Therefore, the appellant-claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,07,309/- as against Rs.1,52,121/-.

The appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.55,188/-
(Rs.2,07,309 - Rs.1,52,121) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of total compensation within Eight Weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.
However, the appellant-claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 170 days, in filing the appeal.

15. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part.
ii.

The impugned judgment and award dated 10.07.2017, passed in M.V.C.No.788/2015, on the file of the Additional District And Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims - 10 - Tribunal, at Kundapura, Udupi District is modified to the aforesaid extent.
